Entries.Text: Generates infusion sets: select base weapon rows, and each enabled infusion adds a row at the base ID + its offset, copied from the base with the infusion's rules applied. Use Learn from Project to build the infusions from the project's existing infused weapons. The settings are saved with the project.
The param the base rows are selected in and the new rows are added to.
The param to generate rows in. Usually EquipParamWeapon.

The ID range one weapon's rows take (its infusions and upgrade rows): 10000 in Elden Ring and Dark Souls III, 1000 in Dark Souls. Only selected rows whose ID is a multiple of it are used as bases, so an already infused row isn't infused again. Learn from Project sets it from the data.
Also generate the rows at base +1 to +99 that exist (per-level upgrade rows, as in Dark Souls), with the same rules. Does nothing where a game has no such rows.
What to do when a row with the new ID already exists.

Add the FMG entries for the new rows, in the primary text language: the title from the infusion's FMG Title template, in the FMG that holds the source's title. A row gets text only when its source has a title. The text is undone from the Text Editor, separately from the rows.
The Text Editor isn't loaded for this project.
Copy the source's other entries of its text entry group (summary, description, ...) to the new ID.
Replace the text of entries that already exist for a new ID. When off, existing entries are left as they are.
Each infusion is one new row per base: its ID offset, its name templates and its rules. Fields without a rule are copied from the base.

Build the infusions from the project's existing infused rows: one per ID offset found on enough weapons. A field gets a Set rule when most infused rows have the same value, an Add rule when most are shifted by the same amount, or a value per weapon type (one of the Group By Fields) when that fits clearly better, as for the status effects of Cold, Poison and Blood. A rule is only kept when it reproduces clearly more rows than leaving the field as it is. The name templates are learned from the row names and titles. Damage and scaling are only learned with Learn Damage and Scaling Rules on.
Replace the current infusions with the learned ones.
No infused rows were found in {0}.
Learned {0} infusions from {1} weapons (ID block {2}), with {3} rules.
Offsets on too few weapons to be infusions were left out: {0}
No infusions. Learn them from the project, or add them yourself.
The infusion's name, used by {infusion} in the templates.
Added to the base row's ID (and to each upgrade row's ID) to get the new row's ID.
{name} is the source's name (its row name, or its title text), {infusion} the infusion's name. For example "{infusion} {name}" or "{name} [{infusion}]". A source without a name gives an empty name.
Every rule reads the base row's values, so their order doesn't matter. Add and Multiply leave a value of -1 (no reference) as it is.
No rules: the rows are copies of the base with the new ID.
The param has no field named {0}, so this rule is skipped.

Set: the field becomes the value. Add: the value is added to the base's value. Multiply: the base's value is multiplied by the value. Scale From: the sum of the base's source fields (set with the cog button) is multiplied by the value, e.g. Fire damage from physical damage. Whole-number fields are rounded.
A number (use . for decimals). Text fields take Set only.
Add a rule to this infusion.
[Param Editor] Weapon Generator rule not applied ({1} rows): {0}
Select the base weapon rows in the target param, then generate.
Open {0} and select the base weapon rows.
{0} new rows for {1} base weapons and {2} infusions.
{0} rows already exist and will be skipped.
{0} selected rows aren't base weapons (their ID isn't a multiple of {1}) and are left out.
Add the rows (one undo step), and the text entries if that option is on (one undo step in the Text Editor).
The rows weren't added: a save is running. Try again when it's done.
Added {0} rows and overwrote {1}, for {2} base weapons.
No text entries were added: the param has no title FMG in the primary text language.
{0} rule applications failed; see the log.

Learn also tries rules for the stat fields, which the games tune per weapon: a fixed value, the base's own value times a factor, another stat field (or the sum of the field's group of stats) times a factor, and each of those with a factor per weapon type. The best one is kept when it reproduces enough of the existing rows; each rule shows how many it fits. Expect close values rather than exact ones.

The fields the stat rules are learned for, separated by commas. * matches any text, and a leading ! leaves the matches out. Fields matched by the same entry form a group that can be summed (e.g. all scaling stats).

The fields a learned rule may use a separate value per group for (e.g. the weapon type), separated by commas. Used for every rule (e.g. the status effect, which depends on the weapon size), and for the damage and scaling rules when that option is on. Fields the param doesn't have are ignored; a grouped rule is only kept when it fits clearly better than an ungrouped one.
The value for base rows whose group isn't listed in the rule's group values (set with the cog button).
Show the rule's source fields (Scale From) and its value per group.
The base row's fields that are added together and multiplied by the value, separated by +. For example "attackBasePhysics" or "correctStrength + correctAgility".
Optional: a field of the base row whose value picks the rule's value from the list below (e.g. a value per weapon type). Rows whose group isn't listed use the rule's own value.
The base row's {0} value this entry is for.
The rule's value for base rows in this group.
Add a value for one group.

Round the result to the nearest whole number, for decimal fields that hold whole numbers such as the scaling stats. Whole-number fields are always rounded. Learn turns it on when the existing infused values of the field are whole numbers.
When it was learned, the share of the project's existing infused rows this rule reproduced (within 1, or 1%). It isn't updated when the rule is edited.
